subject: indoor carbon dioxide
title: What If You Never Opened a Window?

scenes.text: What if you never opened a window? The oxygen wouldn't run out. Your breath would pile up.
Outdoor air holds about 425 parts per million of carbon dioxide. Every breath adds more to the room.
In a closed bedroom overnight, carbon dioxide can climb past 2,000 by morning, and in some rooms past 3,000.
At about 950, office workers in a Harvard study scored 15 percent lower on decision-making tests than in well-ventilated air.
At about 1,400, their scores were 50 percent lower. The air looked and felt exactly the same.
Danish researchers found people slept better and tested better next morning with the window open. The fog was their breath.
